main_body: A tall wooden choir stall: a canopy/cornice on top, a back panel with five arched recesses, and a low seat bench with red cushions across the front
top_band: Rows 8-11 are a brown cornice (L=85-110) with gold finials and a light line at row 12, but this is the front face of the canopy beam. The seat cushions are red strips of 1-2 rows (rows 37-38) with no visible seat surface from above.
evidence: The seat, the part that has to be seen from above, is only a 1-2 row red strip and a thin tan lip (rows 37-40) in front of a flat back panel. The scan at x=24 shows rows 37-38 as red and row 39-40 as a brown lip, so there is no multi-row seat surface. The canopy is a straight front-facing band with no top surface. The arched niches are inset with dark edges, but everything is a vertical face drawn straight on. This is a front elevation, matching the red 'thin seat' and 'front elevation' guides.

style.evidence: The candidate has 11 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 40 and 17-20 for the references, so it is much lower in density. The dark outlines are brown-tinted (0% neutral), so that part is fine. The back panel and recesses are large flat dark-brown fills (rows 16-36 are one tone), with little grain or per-plank texture. The shading has about 4 wood steps against the references' 5-6. It looks flatter and thinner than the cheese stall and the well.
